title: Add Codex SDK MCP subscription gameplay provider
description:
Problem
Eshyra needs a second subscription-backed gameplay provider to spread development and gameplay costs. Codex SDK appears promising because it supports ChatGPT/Codex subscription auth, programmatic control, streamed events, and MCP server integration. Codex is currently blocked by weekly usage limits, so this epic should remain queued/deferred until the adapter seam ADR/refactor lands and usage is available again.

Design Decision
Codex support must follow the API-native vs agent-harness model adapter seam:
- Codex SDK subscription support is an agent-harness adapter.
- OpenAI API-key support is a separate API-native adapter.
- These are not interchangeable auth variants hidden behind one class.
- The Codex subscription adapter must not silently fall back to OpenAI API billing.
- The Codex subscription adapter must not use fenced-text tool calls.

Goal
Implement a Codex subscription-backed gameplay provider using Codex SDK plus Eshyra MCP tools, after the adapter seam is codified and the Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter has established the reference agent-harness pattern.

Scope
1. Confirm the Codex SDK provider mode against the model adapter seam:
   - auth mode: ChatGPT/Codex subscription
   - transport/client: Codex SDK
   - tool transport: MCP
   - turn loop owner: provider-harness-managed
2. Reuse or create an Eshyra MCP tool surface compatible with the Claude Agent SDK MCP pattern where possible.
3. Ensure the Codex harness runs in a sterile environment:
   - temporary working directory, not the Eshyra repo
   - isolated Codex config/home if possible
   - no inherited AGENTS.md/project instructions
   - restrictive sandbox
   - no web/search/network unless explicitly needed
4. Configure only Eshyra MCP tools for gameplay.
5. Map Codex streamed MCP tool-call events into Eshyra debug/transcript records using the same provider-executed-call pattern as the Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter.
6. Delegate all gameplay tool semantics to Eshyra core.
7. Provide manual smoke-test commands for the user to run once Codex usage is available.

Acceptance Criteria
- Codex provider metadata reports subscription auth, Codex SDK transport, agent-harness turn-loop ownership, and MCP tool transport.
- Debug logs show `toolProtocolMode` or equivalent as `codex-mcp`, not fenced text.
- A manual smoke turn requiring a d20 roll causes Codex to invoke the Eshyra MCP `roll` tool.
- No Eshyra repo AGENTS.md/developer instructions are loaded into gameplay context.
- No non-Eshyra tools are available to gameplay, or unavoidable built-ins are documented and proven harmless.
- Failure to access subscription-backed Codex is reported clearly and does not fall back to API key or fenced text.
- API-key OpenAI support remains a separate future adapter mode.

Non-goals
- Do not implement OpenAI API-native support in this epic unless split into a separate child bead.
- Do not replace the Claude Agent SDK adapter.
- Do not remove fenced support repo-wide.
close_reason: Completed: all child and follow-up beads are closed, and local live smoke tests pass.
